Environment configuration MUST rely on documented variables such as `VITE_PRODUCT`, `VITE_STATIC_URL`, `VITE_ACCOUNT_BASE_URL`, `VITE_ACCOUNT_BASE_URL_TEMPLATE`, `ACCOUNT_*`, `AUTHFN_*`, `DATAFN_*`, `DEBUG_SINK_URL`, `DEBUG_SINK_WRITE_TOKEN`, and cloud credentials required by deployment or lookup integrations. Storage, auth, sync, and observability integrations MUST use vetted helpers in `services/account`, `schema`, `client/datafn`, and Superfunctions packages instead of ad-hoc secret handling. Rationale: consistent security practices safeguard users and hosting environments.

## Onboarding Checklist

### Orientation

- Review `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and `WARP.md` before making changes.
- Recognize the monorepo layout:
  - `client/`: SvelteKit frontends, shared client services, features, and product composition.
  - `client/ui/`: Domain-free portable UI package (`@21n/ui`) with `elements`, `compositions`, `actions`, `icons`, `illustrations`, `branding`, `environment`, and `hosts` subpaths.
  - `client/shared-state/`: Product-independent shared Nucleum client state (`@nucleum/shared-state`) grouped by semantic owner, including app context, appearance, commands, events, files, notifications, preferences, resources, and shortcuts.
  - `client/features/`: Multi-product content capabilities (`@nucleum/features`).
  - `client/surfaces/`: Cross-feature product surfaces (`@nucleum/surfaces`): account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, the command surface, and library. Surfaces may compose features; features never import surfaces.
  - `client/shell/`: Application shell (`@nucleum/shell`): navigation, panels, split views, tabs, trails, overlays, modal chrome, and extension-support layers. Base/user application layers live in `client/application`.
  - `client/datafn/`: Client DataFn runtime (`@nucleum/datafn`).
  - `client/application/`: Composition root (`composition/resource-hosts.ts`, `composition/shortcuts.config.ts`), base/user application layers (`layers/`, `paint/` roots), modal orchestration, chrome integration adapters, and product-aware branding.
  - `client/runtime/`: UI-independent browser transport, application environment context, account authority, native messaging, inference, and logging.
  - `client/config/`: Client product identity, declarative navigation metadata, and command identifiers.
  - `services/account/`: account-service AuthFn, DataFn, SearchFn, debug-sink, local Node, and Cloudflare Worker integrations.
  - `schema/`: Product and DataFn schema (`@nucleum/schema`).
  - `shared/`: Cross-layer types and utilities.
  - `apps/`: Deployable product bundles and e2e Playwright harnesses (Memotron, Pointron, Nucleus, Timear, and `apps/e2e-playwright`).
  - `deployment/`: Infrastructure scripts and CDK stacks.
- Confirm product context through `client/products/*` configurations and the app-context store before editing UI flows.

### Ownership and composition

- Read `docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md` and `docs/architecture/type-ownership.md` before changing package ownership or imports. Their current-contract sections are authoritative; historical validation records describe earlier snapshots.
- Preserve the permanent UI dependency direction: compositions may use elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts; elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts MUST NOT depend on compositions. Keep application, runtime, product, feature, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain-state imports out of `client/ui`, including through transitive utility imports.
- Keep a domain-neutral composition in `client/ui/compositions` when it has credible future reuse even if only one feature consumes it today. Usage count alone does not determine ownership. Move only domain-connected adapters, workflows, state access, and product behavior to `client/features` or `client/application`.
- Supply portable UI with data and behavior through explicit props or narrow contracts under `client/ui/hosts`; keep UI-wide platform and presentation state under `client/ui/environment`. Configure both from the owning composition layer. Do not add compatibility wrappers or a generic service locator.
- Keep generic DOM actions in `client/ui/actions`; place capability-specific actions beside their consumer. Consume the package only through its explicit `@21n/ui/elements`, `@21n/ui/compositions`, `@21n/ui/actions`, `@21n/ui/icons`, `@21n/ui/illustrations`, `@21n/ui/branding`, `@21n/ui/environment`, or `@21n/ui/hosts` subpaths. Do not retain empty workspaces or aliases without implemented exports.
- Keep pure logos, provider marks, and illustrations in UI. Branding that selects a product, reads persistence, resolves account/runtime identity, or otherwise performs application behavior belongs in an explicitly named application adapter that composes portable assets through props.
- Portable-looking presentation in the application shell is not automatically shell-owned. Move neutral renderers such as breadcrumbs and scroll containers to `client/ui/compositions`; keep route, history, resource, product, and shell behavior in explicitly named adapters under `client/shell` that pass structural data and callbacks into UI.
- The concrete shell, URL/history navigation, tabs, sidebars, overlays, and product chrome belong in the top-level `client/shell` workspace (`@nucleum/shell`). Features may consume its explicit shell surface when participating in application composition, but MUST NOT import unrelated application workflows. Shell is acyclic: it MUST NOT import application, surfaces, or products directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters only through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`, and concrete chrome (brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status, capture, profile section) enters only through optional Svelte snippet props wired by the application chrome adapters (`client/application/chrome/`).
- Application-wide context belongs to the named `client/shared-state/app-context` owner. Shared command ports and application-event contracts belong in `client/shared-state/commands` and `client/shared-state/events`; command execution infrastructure lives in `client/surfaces/commands`, action definitions stay with their semantic owners, and final registry assembly lives in `client/application/composition`. Runtime environment state belongs in `client/runtime`, persisted UI preference state belongs in `client/shared-state/preferences`, and migration helpers belong in `client/persistence/migrations`. The generic `client/state`, standalone `client/commands`, `client/events`, `client/layout`, `client/branding`, `client/illustrations`, `client/icons`, and `client/iconsV2` directories and their aliases are permanently retired.
- `client/utils` and `@21n/utils` are retired. Colocate helpers and their tests with semantic owners; do not replace them with generic nested utility buckets.
- Do not create a new catch-all `stores`, `state`, `shared`, or `core` directory. The `client/shared-state` workspace is the single approved home for product-independent shared client state and MUST keep named owners with no root barrel or generic dumping at its root. Colocate feature and domain state with its semantic owner. Product-independent client behavior shared by multiple features or products belongs to a named owner under `client/shared-state`, never directly in the shared-state root.
- `@nucleum/shared-state` may depend on lower-level runtime, DataFn, persistence, schema, and portable UI contracts, but MUST NOT depend directly or transitively on application, feature, or product implementations. Features, the shell, products, and application composition may consume explicit shared-state subpaths. Do not add a shared-state root barrel.
- Account state must not own file processing, deletion confirmation, or subscription workflows. Shared uploads belong in `client/shared-state/files`, and user workflows belong in `client/surfaces/account` or `client/surfaces/subscription`.
- Keep generic UI-state persistence in `client/shared-state/preferences`; tabs, sidebar behavior, and product menu customization belong with the application shell. Headless notification and shortcut state belongs in shared-state. Connected notification rendering and global shortcut execution belong under `client/shell`; shortcut settings presentation belongs under `client/surfaces/settings/shortcuts`. The ambiguous top-level `client/application/notifications` and `client/application/shortcuts` directories are retired. Focus owns its scheduled notifications; runtime owns native message delivery.
- Update all callers directly when moving a module. Do not add compatibility re-exports or duplicate entry points. Update feature exports, dependency declarations, retirement rules, and type-inventory destinations with the move.
- Run `npm run check:architecture` and `node tools/check/type-ownership.mjs` for ownership changes. Passing import checks does not replace reviewing semantic ownership or testing workflows.
- Regenerated DataFn mappings must ship with a forward migration when physical database definitions change. Verify both a fresh database and upgrading the checked-in migration history.

### Tooling & Commands

- Use npm workspaces and Turbo tasks; run `npm run dev`, `npm run build`, or filtered commands such as `npm run dev:nucleus` and `npm run build:pointron` when verifying changes.
- Prefer repository scripts over ad-hoc commands to mirror how existing apps are started, built, and tested.

### Local Debugging & Observability

- Use Caddy HTTPS product hosts for browser debugging, not raw localhost, unless the task explicitly targets localhost behavior:
  - Nucleum: `https://local.nucleum.app` -> `localhost:5050`.
  - Pointron: `https://local.pointron.app` -> `localhost:5001`.
  - Memotron: `https://local.memotron.app` -> `localhost:5002`.
- Before diagnosing a local app screen as a frontend bug, verify the account backend is reachable through Caddy. For Nucleum local single-region debugging, start the account service with:
  ```bash
  npm --workspace @21n/account-service run dev:local
  ```
- For cloud-user, login, local-sync, or DataFn failures, check the Caddy-fronted account endpoints first:
  ```bash
  curl -k -i https://account-insouth-local.nucleum.app/auth/session
  curl -k -i -X OPTIONS https://account-insouth-local.nucleum.app/datafn/query \
    -H 'Origin: https://local.nucleum.app' \
    -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST'
  ```
  Healthy local signals include `/auth/session` returning an HTTP response from the account service, DataFn preflights returning `204`, and `access-control-allow-origin: https://local.nucleum.app`.
- Do not confuse the local account API upstream with the debug-sink upstream:
  - `https://account-insouth-local.<product-domain>/debug-sink/*` routes to `localhost:8790`.
  - Normal `/auth/*` and `/datafn/*` account-service traffic routes to `localhost:8787` for `insouth`, `localhost:8788` for `useast`, and `localhost:8789` for `euwest`.
    A `502` on `/auth/session` or `/datafn/*` usually means the account service is not running on the expected account upstream, not that the debug sink is down.
- Debug-sink logging is diagnostic-only and MUST NOT be required for auth or sync behavior. The account service sends debug logs through `DEBUG_SINK_URL` and optional `DEBUG_SINK_WRITE_TOKEN`; production sends nothing without a token. The sink redacts common sensitive fields, but agents MUST still avoid adding logs that expose raw credentials, cookies, OTPs, OAuth codes, tokens, email addresses, private keys, or user content.
- When investigating login, sync, OAuth, or DataFn failures, collect evidence in this order:
  1. Browser console and network status for `/auth/session`, `/auth/regions/lookup`, `/datafn/query`, `/datafn/pull`, `/datafn/push`, and `/datafn/search`.
  2. Account-service terminal logs from `dev:local`.
  3. Caddy route health and upstream port checks.
  4. Database assertions only after the request path is known to be reaching the expected backend.
- For Chrome-extension manual QA, keep using `https://local.nucleum.app` so saved auth state, cookies, CORS, and account authority resolution match the product runtime. Treat raw `http://localhost:5050` auth-shell failures as suspect until reproduced on the local HTTPS product host.

### Coding Standards

- Default to TypeScript, Svelte, and Tailwind conventions already present in the repo.
- Match existing Svelte component organization: `<script lang="ts">`, markup, then `<style>` if needed, with shared logic kept in stores or utilities.
- Keep code free of inline comments per repository policy.
- Add concise JSDoc comments for exported symbols, public APIs, and functions whose purpose or constraints are not immediately obvious from the implementation.
- Honor accessibility and UX patterns by reusing primitives from `@21n/ui/elements` and domain-neutral compositions from `@21n/ui/compositions`. Connect them to preferences, app state, and workflows only from the owning application, shell, or feature layer.
- Follow naming conventions (`camelCase` for functions, `PascalCase` for components, enums colocated with their owning feature, primitive, runtime, or schema).

### Frontend Guidelines

- When editing preferences, use `preferences.save` with the correct `Preference` enum and scoped variables to avoid clobbering user settings.
- Memoize IDs with helpers such as `generateResourceId` and `generateSimpleRandomId` instead of introducing new randomization logic.
- Handle markdown or node manipulation through utilities like `generateMarkdownText` and `NodularMarkdown` instead of new pipelines.
- Respect feature gating via product checks, including comparisons against `Product.NUCLEUM` and `Product.MEMOTRON`.

### Backend & Shared Code

- Backend modules under `services/account/` own AuthFn, account routing, DataFn sync/search, delivery, rate limits, observability, and local/Worker runtime wiring; reuse helpers in `services/account/src`, `schema`, `shared/utils`, and Superfunctions packages instead of duplicating logic.
- When debugging account/auth/DataFn behavior, inspect `services/account/src/app.ts`, `services/account/src/auth.ts`, `services/account/src/debug-sink.ts`, `services/account/src/datafn/`, and `schema/` before changing frontend code.
- Update generated DataFn/Drizzle mappings, schema definitions, and migrations carefully, and coordinate application-side schema expectations with `schema/datafn.ts`.
- Keep shared types with their domain owner in `schema`, `client/features`, `client/runtime`, or `client/datafn`, aligning serialization logic with these definitions before modifying APIs.
- Fix account-service, AuthFn, DataFn, SearchFn, or Superfunctions bugs at their source package rather than masking them in product UI code.

### Testing & Verification

- Run relevant Turbo tasks such as `npm run test`, `npm run lint`, or targeted `turbo run <task> --filter=<project>` after significant changes.
- For UI work, consider Storybook or component-specific verification when available; otherwise smoke test the affected product app.
- Document manual verification steps in pull requests when automated coverage is lacking.

### End-to-End Test Organization

- Organize Playwright suites by shared product capability when the same behavior exists in multiple products. Capability suites such as `tests/focus/` and `tests/memory/` MUST run through product projects and model real product differences through E2E contracts instead of duplicated product-specific specs.
- Keep cross-cutting capability workflows at the capability root and group resource-specific workflows in plural resource directories such as `nodes/`, `objectives/`, and `tasks/`. Resource test directories MUST use plural names.
- Keep a scoped spec at the capability root unless more than two test files clearly belong to the same subdomain. Do not create a nested directory such as `settings/` for one or two specs; use root files such as `settings.spec.ts` instead.
- Centralize repeated capability setup and user workflows in a root helper such as `memory-test-helpers.ts` or `focus-test-helpers.ts`. Keep feature-specific assertions and editor interactions in their owning spec rather than growing a generic helper with unrelated behavior.
- Seed durable precondition state through the E2E DataFn seed fixture (`seed.focus`, `seed.memory`, `seed.collections`) when that state is not the behavior under test. Prefer seed options such as `isPinnedForQuickFocus`, `objectiveId`, and `parentId` over command-bar or panel setup for fixtures. Keep creation, Capture, pin, link, or other setup UI only when that UI path or its side effects is what the test asserts.
- Use Playwright tags only for cross-cutting selection that folder or file paths cannot express. Keep tags such as `@smoke`, `@context-menu`, `@bulk-editor`, `@record-page`, `@creation`, `@browse`, `@settings`, and `@auth`. Do NOT add tags that mirror a directory or file (for example `@focus-feature`, `@session-items`, `@presets`) or capability-scoped smoke/feature aliases such as `@focus-smoke` or `@memory-feature`; select those suites with paths (`tests/focus/`, `tests/focus/active-session/session-items.spec.ts`) and combine with `@smoke` when needed (`tests/focus/ --grep @smoke`).
- Assert immediate user-visible outcomes directly after UI actions: verify the resulting resource, selected bucket, or visible product surface. An action completing, a toast appearing, a store or runtime mutation, or a search result matching is not sufficient proof when stronger visible-state evidence is available.
- Assert DOM readiness and visibility with Playwright web-first locator assertions so UI mode and trace snapshots record the asserted element. For any-of readiness, use `expectAnyLocatorVisible`; for correlated UI conditions, use `expect(...).toPass()` with locator assertions inside. Do not poll `locator.isVisible()` or `locator.isHidden()` booleans.
- Use `expect.poll` only for non-DOM values such as runtime state, persistence, URLs, browser APIs, or serialized collections. Retained polls MUST include a diagnostic `message`; when the polled state has a user-visible consequence, follow it with a direct locator assertion.
- When a workflow writes data that is expected to persist, Playwright tests MUST make both assertions in order: first verify the immediate visible UI feedback, then cross a persistence boundary by closing and reopening the owning page or panel or by reloading the app and navigating back, and verify the durable data again. Do not remove the immediate UI assertion when adding persistence coverage; neither immediate in-memory state nor the post-reopen assertion substitutes for the other.
- Prefer accessible roles, stable test IDs, E2E surface contracts, resource contracts, and shared navigation helpers over CSS structure or product-name branching. Avoid fixed waits where a locator, URL, or persisted-state condition can be awaited.
- Keep specs cohesive and split them when unrelated workflows make ownership or failure diagnosis unclear. Do not copy large specs, repeated route setup, or fallback chains into new resource suites when a shared helper or contract can express the behavior once.

### Workflow Discipline

- Plan work with TODO tracking when tasks involve multiple steps, and close items as progress is made.
- Prefer absolute paths for tooling interactions to avoid ambiguity in the monorepo.
- Use repository-aware tooling, including ripgrep and apply_patch, rather than manual edits that bypass formatting expectations.

### Safety & Secrets

- Never commit environment secrets; rely on documented environment variables such as `VITE_PRODUCT`, `VITE_STATIC_URL`, account-service `ACCOUNT_*` / `AUTHFN_*` / `DATAFN_*` settings, and debug-sink `DEBUG_SINK_*` settings.
- Treat user data and analytics integrations cautiously; consult existing stores or services before changing persistence behavior.

### Additional References

- `WARP.md` for automation policies, CLI workflows, and PR review expectations.
- `deployment/README.md` for infrastructure deployment steps.
- Product-specific docs or configs within `client/products/` for feature toggles and navigation.
- Tests under `tests/`, `apps/e2e-playwright/tests/`, package-local `*.test.ts` files, and fixtures such as `apps/e2e-playwright/tests/fixtures/` to understand existing coverage.
- Always validate assumptions by reading nearby code before rewriting patterns, and ask for clarification when unsure.

## Operational Constraints

- Maintain ASCII-only edits unless files already contain extended characters, never introduce inline comments when modifying code, and prefer JSDoc comments for symbol or function documentation.
- During migrations or refactors, agents MUST NOT introduce intermediary scaffolding, compatibility shims, bridge layers, duplicate config/schema entrypoints, or temporary wrapper APIs unless the user explicitly asks for them. Replace old patterns directly with the target architecture, remove obsolete callers and files in the same change, and stop to ask if a temporary bridge appears unavoidable.

### Non-Negotiable Change Rules

- Any agent fixing issues or bugs, or working on new features, MUST NOT modify existing Playwright or unit tests unless the master explicitly permits each modification.
- Agents MUST NOT modify user-facing UI or functionality unless the master explicitly confirms the change.
- Agents MAY add new Playwright or unit tests when working on new features.

## Workflow Expectations

- Perform code discovery before changes to avoid reimplementing behavior and to understand adjacent systems, especially `client/datafn/`, `client/features/`, `schema/`, `client/persistence`, and `services/account/src/datafn`.
- Align UI updates with accessibility and interaction patterns established in shared components.
- When introducing infrastructure or backend changes, review `deployment/README.md` and coordinate account-service, DataFn, lookup-store, and Cloud deployments with application expectations.
- Record manual verification steps whenever automated coverage is insufficient, ensuring reviewers can reproduce validation.
- Evaluate extension surfaces under `extensions/` whenever share flows or browser integrations are affected to keep host app and extension behavior cohesive.

## Governance

The Tidigit constitution supersedes conflicting process documents for automated agents. Amendments require maintainer approval, an updated Sync Impact Report, and simultaneous updates to dependent templates. Versioning follows semantic rules: MAJOR for principle removals or redefinitions, MINOR for added principles or material scope expansions, PATCH for clarifications. Compliance is reviewed during major feature plans and code reviews; violations must be remediated before merge.

### Sync Impact Report

- Version change: 1.10.1 to 1.11.0.
- Retired client/utils and @21n/utils; colocated helpers and tests with semantic owners.
- Removed workspace/alias/dependency entries and updated architecture enforcement and type inventory.

- Version change: 1.10.0 to 1.10.1.
- Corrected stale command ownership guidance to match the implemented surface runner and application registry assembly.
- Updated application/shell charters and architecture documentation for named transports, account screens, telemetry, sync scheduling and decomposed feature workflows.
- Preserved the existing test and user-facing behavior authorization rules.

- Version change: 1.9.0 to 1.10.0.
- Restricted application source to composition, layers, chrome, branding and paint; retired the remaining workflow and experiment directories.
- Assigned mixed-resource rendering and bulk editing to library, sharing to its surface, OAuth and session resolution to account, diagnostics/errors/support to help, and recovery/update workflows to settings. Modal chrome belongs to shell.
- Extracted runtime host/service-worker/native-message mechanics, shared metadata/timezone/file behavior, and product-configured plan access from application layers. Portable map/capture/quick-access presentation remains in UI with named connected adapters.
- Updated the ownership charters, architecture enforcement, retired-path rules and type-inventory destinations together.

- Version change: 1.8.1 to 1.9.0.
- Made the application shell acyclic: `client/shell` no longer imports `application`, `surfaces`, or `products`; the architecture checker enforces the ban symmetrically with the existing features rule, and the demoted `@nucleum/shell` dependencies on those packages are removed.
- Added the narrow product navigation config host (`client/shared-state/product/product-config-host`, registered from `resource-hosts.ts`) as the only product data the shell reads.
- Injected the five remaining chrome couplings (top nav brand/search/bulk-edit/sync status, left nav profile, app-menu capture) as optional Svelte snippet props wired by the new `client/application/chrome/` adapters; stale paths below are amended accordingly.

- Version change: 1.8.0 to 1.8.1.
- Relocated the base/user application layers (`BaseLayer`, `UserBaseLayer`, `UserLayout`, `AuthGuard`, `ModalLayer`, debug layers), the paint roots (`ComponentResolver`, `AppLoadingView`), and `settingsActionMap` from `client/shell` to `client/application`, since they wire the running product together and were never arrangement-only shell.
- Moved product shortcut defaults (`shortcuts.config.ts`) into `client/application/composition`, already consumed through the `ShortcutHost` contract.
- Relocated `resolveTrialDaysLeft` to `client/runtime/account/plan.utils` and the library resource predicates to `client/shared-state/resources/library.utils`, removing the remaining shell imports of features and subscription surfaces.
- Shell paint resolvers now render named actions through the shared-state action renderer host instead of importing application composition directly.

- Version change: 1.7.0 to 1.8.0.
- Renamed the shared client state workspace from `client/capabilities` to `client/shared-state` (`@nucleum/shared-state`), approving that name as the single shared-state home while retaining the named-owner and no-root-barrel rules.
- Lifted the application shell to the top-level `client/shell` workspace (`@nucleum/shell`); it remains the only app-level layer features may consume.
- Established the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`) for cross-feature product surfaces (account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, command, search, library) and enforced that features never import surfaces.
- Narrowed `client/application` toward the composition root, modal orchestration, record presentation, and app-specific integrations.
- Synchronized the architecture references and per-layer charter READMEs; retained existing test and UI authorization rules.

**Version**: 1.11.0 | **Ratified**: 2025-09-27 | **Last Amended**: 2026-09-22

# Client ownership and import boundaries

Tracked in [TIDY-477](https://linear.app/21n/issue/TIDY-477/enforce-architectural-boundaries-after-client-feature-and-datafn).

## Delivery checklist

- [x] Commit the existing reorganization separately from schema, session, and popover fixes.
- [x] Move shared focus preferences and sound state into focus ownership, retaining persistence keys.
- [x] Remove the composition/session-store cycle by passing fixed end times explicitly.
- [x] Move memory upload, search-result, and synced-id helpers out of product implementations.
- [x] Supply the graph layout from the product shell.
- [x] Move authentication, network authority, connectivity, and logging into non-UI runtime ownership.
- [x] Move the active-resource UI store out of DataFn and avatar/icon catalogs into UI ownership and initial app data into configuration.
- [x] Remove unused mutation-label helpers from DataFn and depend on the observable-store interface instead of its implementation.
- [x] Move shared product contracts and navigation metadata out of product implementations.
- [x] Enforce completed boundaries and declare existing public feature entry points.
- [x] Pass compiler checks for Nucleum, Pointron, Memotron, and account-service.
- [x] Pass seven schema tests, two focus-preferences tests, and three popover tests.
- [x] Pass four Nucleum focus browser scenarios with no page errors.
- [x] Update the approved existing-test import and mock paths.
- [x] Adapt the approved fixed-end-time test setup without changing expected durations; pass 127 tests across all 19 affected unit-test files.
- [x] Confirm Playwright discovers all 549 tests in 55 files after import updates.

## Ownership

`schema` owns resource definitions. `client/datafn` owns the client storage and sync runtime. `client/runtime` owns browser infrastructure such as account transport, network authority, connectivity, and diagnostic logging. `client/features` owns capability implementations. `client/products` composes those capabilities into product experiences. Client product identity composition lives in `client/config/product.type.ts`; cross-layer product identity lives in `schema/product.type.ts`; declarative navigation metadata lives in `client/config`.

`client/ui` is the permanent domain-free `@21n/ui` package. `elements` owns atomic controls and UI-only types. `compositions` owns domain-neutral compound UI intended for present or future reuse, including charts, maps, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, file presentation, keyboard listeners, duration inputs, scroll containers, and time selectors. `actions` owns generic DOM behavior, `icons` owns portable icon assets and rendering, `illustrations` owns portable artwork, and `branding` owns pure visual brand assets. Package-wide portable platform state belongs to `environment`, while dependency-inversion contracts shared across controls and compositions belong to `hosts`. A single current consumer does not make a composition feature-owned. `client/shell` (`@nucleum/shell`) owns the concrete product shell: navigation, panels, split views, tabs, trails, overlays, modal chrome, and the extension-support layers. `client/surfaces` (`@nucleum/surfaces`) owns cross-feature product surfaces: account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, the command surface (`commandBar`, `commands`, `search`), and `library` resource browsing. `client/application` retains the composition root (`composition/resource-hosts.ts`, `composition/shortcuts.config.ts`), the base/user application layers, modal orchestration, chrome integration adapters, and product-aware branding adapters. Markdown editing and tags belong to memory; combinations belong to spaces. Product-independent shared client behavior lives in the `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace under explicit `app-context`, `appearance`, `commands`, `events`, `files`, `notifications`, `preferences`, `product`, `resources`, and `shortcuts` owners. Cross-layer billing contracts live in `schema/account`. Keyboard and interaction-mode contracts live in `client/ui/elements/keyboard`; panel and error presentation contracts live in their capability owners. See [type ownership](type-ownership.md) for the complete inventory.

## Enforced rules

Run `npm run check:architecture`. CI and the root lint command run the same check. It resolves relative imports, source aliases, dynamic imports, and TypeScript import types in TypeScript and Svelte scripts.

- Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition; the top-level shell is the only app-level layer features may consume. Surfaces may compose features; features must never import surfaces.
- Surfaces must not import application composition. Product presentation and action rendering enter surfaces through narrow shared-state hosts installed by application composition.
- The application shell is acyclic: `client/shell` must not import application, surfaces, or products, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters only through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome (brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status, capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props wired by the application chrome adapters (`client/application/chrome/`).
- Portable UI cannot directly or transitively import application state, runtime, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, or domain state.
- Compositions may use elements, actions, environment, and hosts; those lower UI layers cannot import compositions.
- Shared state cannot directly or transitively import application, feature, or product implementations.
- DataFn and runtime files cannot directly import features, products, application composition or shell, portable UI, or shared client state and services.
- Composition calculations cannot import the session singleton.
- A caller outside a capability must use a source file explicitly listed in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`.

The feature entry-point list records the existing public surface, including individual components and type modules; it is not a barrel module. Additions require an explicit contract change. Package exports expose these same paths. Source aliases bypass package exports, which is why the source-level check remains necessary.

## Current architecture contract

Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition. The application shell is the top-level `client/shell` workspace (`@nucleum/shell`), the only app-level layer features may consume. Cross-feature product surfaces live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`); surfaces may compose features, while features never import surfaces. The portable UI foundation is the single `client/ui` workspace, consumed through `@21n/ui/elements`, `@21n/ui/compositions`, `@21n/ui/actions`, `@21n/ui/icons`, `@21n/ui/illustrations`, `@21n/ui/branding`, `@21n/ui/environment`, and `@21n/ui/hosts`. Compositions may use the other UI layers, while elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts never depend on compositions. The entire package remains independent, directly and transitively, from application state, runtime infrastructure, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Domain-neutral compositions stay in UI when future shared use is intentional, even with one current consumer. Product-connected behavior enters through explicit props or narrow contracts under `client/ui/hosts`, configured from `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts` or supplied by the owning shell or feature adapter. Shared state and utilities cannot transitively load application or feature composition at runtime. Explicit type-only edges are excluded from the shared-runtime reachability rule; cross-capability imports remain permitted through declared public entries, so the complete source graph is not claimed to be acyclic.

`client/shared-state` is the single `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace. It groups product-independent Nucleum client behavior by semantic owner without turning `client/` into a list of service folders. Shared command ports and application events are shared state because they are consumed across features, products, extensions, and application composition; concrete command execution remains application-owned. Shared state may consume lower-level runtime, DataFn, persistence, schema, utilities, and portable UI contracts. They may not consume application workflows or shell implementations, user-facing feature implementations, or product composition, directly or transitively. Consumers import named subpaths such as `@nucleum/shared-state/preferences/preferences.store`; there is no root barrel, `shared`, `core`, generic `state`, or nested generic `stores` bucket.

Focus and memory event contracts live under `client/shared-state/events`; clipper
transport events live under `client/runtime/extensions`. App metadata belongs to
`client/shared-state/app-context`. Surfaces consume application-selected action
rendering and product visuals through named shared-state hosts.

Presentation ownership is separate from navigation ownership. Neutral breadcrumbs and scroll containers live in UI. `client/shell/navigation/components/AppBreadcrumbs.svelte` translates application resource and path metadata into structural breadcrumb items and callbacks. Sidebars, tabs, split views, panels, and trails remain in the application shell when they own URL state, resource resolution, product menus, shell events, or other application orchestration. A component moves to UI only when its public contract can be expressed without product or domain vocabulary.

Application and extension shells configure permanent overlay, resource-action, panel, shortcut, recents, record-renderer, action-renderer, portable action, shortcut, file, environment, logging, and haptic contracts in `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts`. Configuration runs from base, user, and extension shells before presentation or command execution. Shell and feature adapters provide view-specific props such as keyboard matching, time scales, and address resolution. Shared Markdown display owns portable parsing; memory owns Markdown editing. Portable file presentation, resource enums, event contracts, and action identifiers no longer depend on capability implementations.

The public feature API is enumerated in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`. Each has a static consumer outside its capability. The checker rejects unused public entries and private external imports. This reduces the previous 154 entries by moving shared contracts and infrastructure to their proper owners without introducing barrels or compatibility paths.

Registered workspaces declare their production source imports. `@nucleum/client` owns lower-level config and runtime; `@nucleum/shared-state` owns product-independent shared client behavior, application context, command ports, and events; `@nucleum/shell` owns the application shell; `@nucleum/surfaces` owns cross-feature product surfaces; `@21n/ui` owns all portable presentation and visual assets. Source workspaces bundled by an app declare co-hosted workspace requirements as peer dependencies; existing build dependencies remain dependencies. Peers describe the host's source compilation requirements without adding artificial Turbo build cycles. This is not a claim that each source package builds or installs independently. The checker verifies both resolved workspace and external package imports; test and story dependencies are outside this production-source check.

`schema` owns resource definitions. `client/datafn` owns the client storage and sync runtime. `client/runtime` owns browser infrastructure such as account transport, network authority, connectivity, and diagnostic logging. `client/features` owns capability implementations. `client/products` composes those capabilities into product experiences. `client/ui` is the permanent domain-free `@21n/ui` package. `elements` owns atomic controls and UI-only types. `compositions` owns domain-neutral compound UI intended for present or future reuse, including charts, maps, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, file presentation, keyboard listeners, duration inputs, scroll containers, and time selectors. `actions` owns generic DOM behavior, `icons` owns portable icon assets and rendering, `illustrations` owns portable artwork, and `branding` owns pure visual brand assets. Package-wide portable platform state belongs to `environment`, while dependency-inversion contracts shared across controls and compositions belong to `hosts`. A single current consumer does not make a composition feature-owned. `client/shell` (`@nucleum/shell`) owns the concrete product shell: navigation, panels, split views, tabs, trails, overlays, modal chrome, and the extension-support layers. `client/surfaces` (`@nucleum/surfaces`) owns cross-feature product surfaces: account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, the command surface (`commandBar`, `commands`, `search`), and `library` resource browsing. `client/application` retains the composition root (`composition/resource-hosts.ts`, `composition/shortcuts.config.ts`), the base/user application layers, modal orchestration, chrome integration adapters, and product-aware branding adapters. Product-independent shared client behavior lives in the `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace under explicit `app-context`, `appearance`, `commands`, `events`, `files`, `notifications`, `preferences`, `product`, `resources`, and `shortcuts` owners. Run `npm run check:architecture`. CI and the root lint command run the same check. It resolves relative imports, source aliases, dynamic imports, and TypeScript import types in TypeScript and Svelte scripts.

- Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition; the top-level shell is the only app-level layer features may consume. Surfaces may compose features; features must never import surfaces.
- Surfaces must not import application composition. Product presentation and action rendering enter surfaces through narrow shared-state hosts installed by application composition.
- The application shell is acyclic: `client/shell` must not import application, surfaces, or products, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters only through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome (brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status, capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props wired by the application chrome adapters (`client/application/chrome/`).
- Portable UI cannot directly or transitively import application state, runtime, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, or domain state.
- Compositions may use elements, actions, environment, and hosts; those lower UI layers cannot import compositions.
- Shared state cannot directly or transitively import application, feature, or product implementations.
- DataFn and runtime files cannot directly import features, products, application composition or shell, portable UI, or shared client state and services.
- Composition calculations cannot import the session singleton.
- A caller outside a capability must use a source file explicitly listed in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`.

The feature entry-point list records the existing public surface, including individual components and type modules; it is not a barrel module. Additions require an explicit contract change. Package exports expose these same paths. Source aliases bypass package exports, which is why the source-level check remains necessary.

## Current architecture contract

Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition. The application shell is the top-level `client/shell` workspace (`@nucleum/shell`), the only app-level layer features may consume. Cross-feature product surfaces live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`); surfaces may compose features, while features never import surfaces. The portable UI foundation is the single `client/ui` workspace, consumed through `@21n/ui/elements`, `@21n/ui/compositions`, `@21n/ui/actions`, `@21n/ui/icons`, `@21n/ui/illustrations`, `@21n/ui/branding`, `@21n/ui/environment`, and `@21n/ui/hosts`. Compositions may use the other UI layers, while elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts never depend on compositions. The entire package remains independent, directly and transitively, from application state, runtime infrastructure, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Domain-neutral compositions stay in UI when future shared use is intentional, even with one current consumer. Product-connected behavior enters through explicit props or narrow contracts under `client/ui/hosts`, configured from `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts` or supplied by the owning shell or feature adapter. Shared state and utilities cannot transitively load application or feature composition at runtime. Explicit type-only edges are excluded from the shared-runtime reachability rule; cross-capability imports remain permitted through declared public entries, so the complete source graph is not claimed to be acyclic.

`client/shared-state` is the single `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace. It groups product-independent Nucleum client behavior by semantic owner without turning `client/` into a list of service folders. Shared command ports and application events are shared state because they are consumed across features, products, extensions, and application composition; concrete command execution remains application-owned. Shared state may consume lower-level runtime, DataFn, persistence, schema, utilities, and portable UI contracts. They may not consume application workflows or shell implementations, user-facing feature implementations, or product composition, directly or transitively. Consumers import named subpaths such as `@nucleum/shared-state/preferences/preferences.store`; there is no root barrel, `shared`, `core`, generic `state`, or nested generic `stores` bucket.

Focus and memory event contracts live under `client/shared-state/events`; clipper
transport events live under `client/runtime/extensions`. App metadata belongs to
`client/shared-state/app-context`. Surfaces consume application-selected action
rendering and product visuals through named shared-state hosts.

Presentation ownership is separate from navigation ownership. Neutral breadcrumbs and scroll containers live in UI. `client/shell/navigation/components/AppBreadcrumbs.svelte` translates application resource and path metadata into structural breadcrumb items and callbacks. Sidebars, tabs, split views, panels, and trails remain in the application shell when they own URL state, resource resolution, product menus, shell events, or other application orchestration. A component moves to UI only when its public contract can be expressed without product or domain vocabulary.

Application and extension shells configure permanent overlay, resource-action, panel, shortcut, recents, record-renderer, action-renderer, portable action, shortcut, file, environment, logging, and haptic contracts in `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts`. Configuration runs from base, user, and extension shells before presentation or command execution. # Type and contract ownership

## Conventions

Definitions stay beside their implementation unless independent consumers need a neutral contract. Feature contracts belong to the feature and external callers use explicit public entries. Those contracts must not derive from schema records, DataFn resources, runtime types, application actions, or state interfaces; owning adapters translate domain models at the UI boundary. Keyboard contracts are shared by controls and application shortcuts. Application action contracts belong to client configuration; shared command-host and event contracts belong to `client/shared-state/commands` and `client/shared-state/events`; resource-panel and notification models belong to their named capabilities. Browser ambient declarations live in client/ambient.

Schema owns cross-layer account, subscription, and legacy persistence wire contracts. Shared account contracts must not import client modules. Legacy serialized formats remain distinct from current DataFn records: deriving them from a newer schema would change their accepted shape. Generated AuthFn and DataFn/Drizzle files remain owned by services/account generation scripts and are never manually rewritten. Type-only dependencies use import type; enums used at runtime retain value imports.

The global client/types and shared/types packages are retired, without replacement catch-all packages or compatibility exports. Splits use direct imports to the actual owner. Billing presentation fields remain in surfaces/subscription; wire enums and billing data belong to schema/account. Store interfaces are separated from legacy mutation/filter wire contracts. Markdown validation and responsive text truncation leave shared utilities for their frontend owners.

Product menu contracts live in `client/shell/navigation/app-menu.type.ts`. The inventory retains original paths as baseline provenance and updates destinations for current ownership. Portable UI, including both former icon systems, illustrations, and pure branding assets, is consolidated in the `@21n/ui` workspace, and the old elements, components, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, layout, state, and stores workspace aliases are retired. Product-independent cross-capability state, command ports, events, and services use named owners under `client/shared-state`; runtime context, persistent UI preferences, migrations, shell state, and product-aware branding adapters are colocated with their semantic owners. Historical manifest and alias snapshots remain as evidence; `currentPackages` records the 30 current manifests. `@nucleum/client`, `@nucleum/shared-state`, and `@21n/ui` are registered private source workspaces and are not independently publishable builds.

The empty legacy and catch-all client utility workspaces have since been retired; `currentPackages` now records 30 manifests. Reproduce the browser checks with `node apps/e2e-playwright/scripts/probe-review-session.mjs` and `node apps/e2e-playwright/scripts/probe-markdown-ownership.mjs` while the local product server is running. Neither requires existing user data; each runs in a fresh offline browser context. Full cross-product Playwright, live auth/sync, native app packaging and production deployment were not exercised.

## Historical overlay/resource ownership refinement

TIDY-477 originally moved reusable popup contracts to the then-current elements package, overlay state to the then-current stores workspace, active-resource/selection state to its resource group, and generic ResourceError to DataFn. # Client ownership and import boundaries

Tracked in [TIDY-477](https://linear.app/21n/issue/TIDY-477/enforce-architectural-boundaries-after-client-feature-and-datafn).

## Delivery checklist

- [x] Commit the existing reorganization separately from schema, session, and popover fixes.
- [x] Move shared focus preferences and sound state into focus ownership, retaining persistence keys.
- [x] Remove the composition/session-store cycle by passing fixed end times explicitly.
- [x] Move memory upload, search-result, and synced-id helpers out of product implementations.
- [x] Supply the graph layout from the product shell.
- [x] Move authentication, network authority, connectivity, and logging into non-UI runtime ownership.
- [x] Move the active-resource UI store out of DataFn and avatar/icon catalogs into UI ownership and initial app data into configuration.
- [x] Remove unused mutation-label helpers from DataFn and depend on the observable-store interface instead of its implementation.

- [x] Adapt the approved fixed-end-time test setup without changing expected durations; pass 127 tests across all 19 affected unit-test files.
- [x] Confirm Playwright discovers all 549 tests in 55 files after import updates.

## Ownership

`schema` owns resource definitions. `client/datafn` owns the client storage and sync runtime. `client/runtime` owns browser infrastructure such as account transport, network authority, connectivity, and diagnostic logging. `client/features` owns capability implementations. `client/products` composes those capabilities into product experiences. Client product identity composition lives in `client/config/product.type.ts`; cross-layer product identity lives in `schema/product.type.ts`; declarative navigation metadata lives in `client/config`.

`client/ui` is the permanent domain-free `@21n/ui` package. `elements` owns atomic controls and UI-only types. `compositions` owns domain-neutral compound UI intended for present or future reuse, including charts, maps, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, file presentation, keyboard listeners, duration inputs, scroll containers, and time selectors. `actions` owns generic DOM behavior, `icons` owns portable icon assets and rendering, `illustrations` owns portable artwork, and `branding` owns pure visual brand assets. Package-wide portable platform state belongs to `environment`, while dependency-inversion contracts shared across controls and compositions belong to `hosts`. A single current consumer does not make a composition feature-owned. `client/shell` (`@nucleum/shell`) owns the concrete product shell: navigation, panels, split views, tabs, trails, overlays, modal chrome, and the extension-support layers. `client/surfaces` (`@nucleum/surfaces`) owns cross-feature product surfaces: account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, the command surface (`commandBar`, `commands`, `search`), and `library` resource browsing. `client/application` retains the composition root (`composition/resource-hosts.ts`, `composition/shortcuts.config.ts`), the base/user application layers, modal orchestration, chrome integration adapters, and product-aware branding adapters. Markdown editing and tags belong to memory; combinations belong to spaces. Product-independent shared client behavior lives in the `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace under explicit `app-context`, `appearance`, `commands`, `events`, `files`, `notifications`, `preferences`, `product`, `resources`, and `shortcuts` owners. Cross-layer billing contracts live in `schema/account`. Keyboard and interaction-mode contracts live in `client/ui/elements/keyboard`; panel and error presentation contracts live in their capability owners. See [type ownership](type-ownership.md) for the complete inventory.

## Enforced rules

Run `npm run check:architecture`. CI and the root lint command run the same check. It resolves relative imports, source aliases, dynamic imports, and TypeScript import types in TypeScript and Svelte scripts.

- Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition; the top-level shell is the only app-level layer features may consume. Surfaces may compose features; features must never import surfaces.
- Surfaces must not import application composition. Product presentation and action rendering enter surfaces through narrow shared-state hosts installed by application composition.
- The application shell is acyclic: `client/shell` must not import application, surfaces, or products, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters only through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome (brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status, capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props wired by the application chrome adapters (`client/application/chrome/`).
- Portable UI cannot directly or transitively import application state, runtime, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, or domain state.
- Compositions may use elements, actions, environment, and hosts; those lower UI layers cannot import compositions.
- Shared state cannot directly or transitively import application, feature, or product implementations.
- DataFn and runtime files cannot directly import features, products, application composition or shell, portable UI, or shared client state and services.
- Composition calculations cannot import the session singleton.
- A caller outside a capability must use a source file explicitly listed in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`.

The feature entry-point list records the existing public surface, including individual components and type modules; it is not a barrel module. Additions require an explicit contract change. Package exports expose these same paths. Source aliases bypass package exports, which is why the source-level check remains necessary.

## Current architecture contract

Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition. The application shell is the top-level `client/shell` workspace (`@nucleum/shell`), the only app-level layer features may consume. Cross-feature product surfaces live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`); surfaces may compose features, while features never import surfaces. The portable UI foundation is the single `client/ui` workspace, consumed through `@21n/ui/elements`, `@21n/ui/compositions`, `@21n/ui/actions`, `@21n/ui/icons`, `@21n/ui/illustrations`, `@21n/ui/branding`, `@21n/ui/environment`, and `@21n/ui/hosts`. Compositions may use the other UI layers, while elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts never depend on compositions. The entire package remains independent, directly and transitively, from application state, runtime infrastructure, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Domain-neutral compositions stay in UI when future shared use is intentional, even with one current consumer. Product-connected behavior enters through explicit props or narrow contracts under `client/ui/hosts`, configured from `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts` or supplied by the owning shell or feature adapter. Shared state and utilities cannot transitively load application or feature composition at runtime. Explicit type-only edges are excluded from the shared-runtime reachability rule; cross-capability imports remain permitted through declared public entries, so the complete source graph is not claimed to be acyclic.

`client/shared-state` is the single `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace. It groups product-independent Nucleum client behavior by semantic owner without turning `client/` into a list of service folders. Shared command ports and application events are shared state because they are consumed across features, products, extensions, and application composition; concrete command execution remains application-owned. Shared state may consume lower-level runtime, DataFn, persistence, schema, utilities, and portable UI contracts. They may not consume application workflows or shell implementations, user-facing feature implementations, or product composition, directly or transitively. Consumers import named subpaths such as `@nucleum/shared-state/preferences/preferences.store`; there is no root barrel, `shared`, `core`, generic `state`, or nested generic `stores` bucket.

Focus and memory event contracts live under `client/shared-state/events`; clipper
transport events live under `client/runtime/extensions`. App metadata belongs to
`client/shared-state/app-context`. Surfaces consume application-selected action
rendering and product visuals through named shared-state hosts.

Presentation ownership is separate from navigation ownership. Neutral breadcrumbs and scroll containers live in UI. `client/shell/navigation/components/AppBreadcrumbs.svelte` translates application resource and path metadata into structural breadcrumb items and callbacks. Sidebars, tabs, split views, panels, and trails remain in the application shell when they own URL state, resource resolution, product menus, shell events, or other application orchestration. A component moves to UI only when its public contract can be expressed without product or domain vocabulary.

Application and extension shells configure permanent overlay, resource-action, panel, shortcut, recents, record-renderer, action-renderer, portable action, shortcut, file, environment, logging, and haptic contracts in `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts`. Configuration runs from base, user, and extension shells before presentation or command execution. Shell and feature adapters provide view-specific props such as keyboard matching, time scales, and address resolution. Shared Markdown display owns portable parsing; memory owns Markdown editing. Portable file presentation, resource enums, event contracts, and action identifiers no longer depend on capability implementations.

The public feature API is enumerated in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`. Each has a static consumer outside its capability. The checker rejects unused public entries and private external imports. This reduces the previous 154 entries by moving shared contracts and infrastructure to their proper owners without introducing barrels or compatibility paths.

Registered workspaces declare their production source imports. `@nucleum/client` owns lower-level config and runtime; `@nucleum/shared-state` owns product-independent shared client behavior, application context, command ports, and events; `@nucleum/shell` owns the application shell; `@nucleum/surfaces` owns cross-feature product surfaces; `@21n/ui` owns all portable presentation and visual assets. Source workspaces bundled by an app declare co-hosted workspace requirements as peer dependencies; existing build dependencies remain dependencies. Peers describe the host's source compilation requirements without adding artificial Turbo build cycles. This is not a claim that each source package builds or installs independently. The checker verifies both resolved workspace and external package imports; test and story dependencies are outside this production-source check.

The narrow Library now mounts resource panes only after a resource is selected. A dedicated focus-capability test covers the portrait Library in Nucleum and Pointron; a seeded Recents probe verifies visibility before and after reload without page errors. Broader regression results are recorded below separately from the architecture checks.

## Application-state ownership follow-up

Product and application context lives in `client/shared-state/app-context/app.store.ts`. Browser/embed environment context lives in `client/runtime/context.store.ts`; persistent UI preference state lives in `client/shared-state/preferences/ui-state`; legacy product-key migration belongs to `client/persistence/migrations`. URL/history and resource navigation live in `client/shell/navigation/navigation.ts`. Product command lookup/execution lives in `client/surfaces/commands/action-runner.ts`; the permanent shared `CommandHost` contract lives in `client/shared-state/commands/command-host.ts` and is installed from `resource-hosts.ts`. Application-wide events live in `client/shared-state/events`. No old methods delegate to the new owners.

Reactive account session state lives with the account runtime in `client/runtime/account/account.store.ts`. Authentication persistence, bootstrap, sign-in, sign-out, navigation, and DataFn teardown are coordinated by `client/surfaces/account/account-session.ts`. Deletion confirmation and cleanup orchestration live in `client/surfaces/account/account-deletion.ts`; subscription operations live in `client/surfaces/subscription/subscription.ts`; file conversion, thumbnail generation, signing, and local/remote storage live in `client/shared-state/files/file-upload.ts`. OAuth initiation and callback presentation belong to surfaces/account; legacy code exchange belongs to runtime/account.

The connected offline-status indicator lives in `client/application/chrome`; shared elements and the shell do not read account session state. Application composition supplies the indicator to shell chrome.

Product menu persistence lives beside navigation. Tab and sidebar mutations live beside the application shell; generic UI-state persistence belongs to the preferences capability. Shortcut persistence, matching, hints, and the host contract live in `client/shared-state/shortcuts`; global shortcut execution lives in `client/shell/shortcuts`, and shortcut settings presentation lives in `client/surfaces/settings/shortcuts`. Headless notification state lives in `client/shared-state/notifications`, while connected notification rendering lives in `client/shell/notifications`. Focus owns its scheduled notification queue, and the existing native transport delivers messages. Memory owns its word-count and PDF-overlay DOM actions. The unused Markdown action and empty `@nucleum/cx` workspace are retired, including active aliases and workspace declarations.

The former `client/stores`, `client/state`, `client/commands`, and `client/events` directories are retired. App context, appearance, commands, events, files, notifications, preferences, resources, and shortcuts have explicit owners under `client/shared-state`. Runtime environment state belongs to runtime, migration state belongs to persistence, the observable-store implementation belongs to DataFn, and overlay state belongs to the application shell. New state follows semantic ownership and must not recreate a catch-all `stores`, `state`, `shared`, or `core` directory; `client/shared-state` is the single approved shared-state workspace and keeps named owners with no root barrel.

Connected record menus and bulk mutations live in `client/features/records`; shared-state/resources retains selection state and the resource action host contract. DataFn resource selection, storage lifecycle, runtime policy and remote transport have named modules; `datafn.store.ts` owns the live client and lifecycle. Persistence separates client storage, device identity, legacy local storage, and the named legacy-backup operations. URL validation and product host parsing have named cross-layer utilities; memory owns its embed sanitizer, and the legacy Surreal query builder lives with server sync.

## Application composition refinement

`client/utils` and `@21n/utils` are retired, including their workspace and aliases.
Date arithmetic, parsing, period contracts, timezone lookup, user-date calculation
and file-size conversion are domain-free named modules under `shared/utils`.
Duration presentation belongs to UI time controls, chart formatting to chart
compositions, contextual events to UI environment, and color presentation to
theme. Focus owns session-item ordering; shell owns the existing touch-navigation
behavior. Extension transport lives in runtime/extensions, extension navigation
in client/extensions, PDF previews in shared-state/files, migration tracking in

See the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for details. ### Contact For any questions, security reporting or feedback, please contact us at [hello@21n.co](mailto:hello@21n.co). ❤️ We extend our deepest gratitude to all the [OSS libraries and tools](https://github.com/21nOrg/nucleus/network/dependencies) that made this project possible. ## Code organization Product bundles in `apps/` compose user-facing features from `client/features/`. `client/ui/` is the domain-free, portable `@21n/ui` package: `elements` owns atomic controls, `compositions` owns reusable compound UI such as charts, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, and time controls, `actions` owns generic DOM behavior, `icons` owns portable icon assets and rendering, `illustrations` owns portable artwork, `branding` owns pure visual brand assets, and `environment` plus `hosts` provide package-wide integration contracts. Product-independent Nucleum behavior shared across features or products lives in named subdirectories of `client/shared-state/` and is imported from `@nucleum/shared-state/*`, including command ports and application events; this package must not depend on application, feature, or product implementations. `schema/` owns cross-layer contracts, `client/datafn/` owns storage and sync, and `services/account/` owns the backend. Application composition lives in `client/application/`; account, settings, sharing, library and other workflows live in `client/surfaces/`; navigation, notification presentation and shortcut execution live in `client/shell`; UI-independent infrastructure lives in `client/runtime/`. State is colocated with app context, runtime, preferences, persistence, shell, or feature owners rather than a generic `client/state` directory. See [client boundaries](docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md) for the current ownership model, [type ownership](docs/architecture/type-ownership.md) for contracts, and [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for maintainer orientation. # Contributor and maintainer orientation As noted in README.md, external contributions are not currently accepted. This guide documents the workflow for maintainers and authorized agents. Start with [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), [WARP.md](WARP.md), [client boundaries](docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md), and [type ownership](docs/architecture/type-ownership.md). Confirm the active product in `client/products` and `client/config`. UI-wide platform state and dependency-inversion contracts belong to `@21n/ui/environment` and `@21n/ui/hosts`, not under an individual element. Keep a composition shared when credible future reuse is intentional even if it currently has one consumer. The entire UI package must remain independent of application state, runtime, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state; inject product behavior through props or narrow host contracts. Keep product-aware branding and other connected adapters with application composition. The concrete application shell lives under `client/shell`; the generic `client/layout`, `client/branding`, `client/illustrations`, `client/icons`, `client/iconsV2`, `client/commands`, `client/events`, and `client/state` owners are retired. Connected notification rendering and shortcut execution belong to the shell, while shortcut settings UI belongs under `client/surfaces/settings/shortcuts`. Use repository scripts for setup, compilation, tests, and builds. Run architecture and type-ownership checks for moves, and include a forward migration when generated database mappings change. Do not modify existing tests without the per-file authorization required by AGENTS.md. PRs should describe the user-visible result, ownership changes, checks performed, and limitations. Do not include secrets, local environment files, build output, or unrelated workspace changes. # Repository guide `AGENTS.md` is the governing agent policy. Read it before changes. The current architecture is documented in [client boundaries](docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md) and [type ownership](docs/architecture/type-ownership.md). ## Organization - `schema/`: cross-layer product/resource definitions, wire contracts, and legacy serialization contracts. - `client/datafn/`: client storage, queries, sync, and DataFn resource adapters. - `client/runtime/`: UI-independent auth/account transport, connectivity, logging, native messaging, audio, and inference. - `client/features/`: shared capabilities such as memory, focus, calendar, collections, and spaces. - `client/products/`: product-specific composition, configuration, and integrations. - `client/config/`: client product identity, navigation metadata, and command identifiers. - `client/application/`: composition, lifecycle orchestration, chrome/branding adapters, and startup/action rendering. - `client/surfaces/`: account, subscription, settings, help, sharing, command and library workflows. - `client/shell/`: navigation, panels, tabs, modal chrome, viewport behavior and connected shell presentation. - `client/ui/`: the domain-free `@21n/ui` package. Import atomic controls from `@21n/ui/elements`, reusable compound UI from `@21n/ui/compositions`, generic DOM behavior from `@21n/ui/actions`, portable icons from `@21n/ui/icons`, illustrations from `@21n/ui/illustrations`, pure visual brand assets from `@21n/ui/branding`, portable platform state from `@21n/ui/environment`, and host contracts from `@21n/ui/hosts`. - `client/shared-state/`: the product-independent `@nucleum/shared-state` package with named app-context, appearance, commands, events, files, notifications, preferences, resources, and shortcuts owners. - `client/persistence/`: persistence helpers and legacy backup/recovery boundaries. - `services/account/`: AuthFn/DataFn account service, database mappings, lookup integrations, and Node/Worker deployments. - `shared/`: cross-layer utilities and remaining legacy database objects. - `apps/`, `extensions/`: deployable product and extension bundles; `apps/e2e-playwright` owns browser verification. There is no global `client/types`, `shared/types`, or `client/utils` package. Helpers and tests follow their semantic owners; `@21n/utils` is retired. Import contracts from their domain owner. The unused `@nucleum/cx` workspace is retired. ## Composition rules App context does not implement navigation or command execution. Shared state exposes the command port; `client/surfaces/commands` executes commands whose definitions live with their semantic owners and whose ordered registry is assembled in application composition. The application shell changes URL/history and owns connected notification rendering plus global shortcut execution. Shortcut settings presentation belongs under `client/surfaces/settings/shortcuts`. Application and extension shells install command, overlay, resource, renderer, shortcut, recents, icon-asset, and UI-environment hosts through `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts` before mounting consumers. Compositions may use elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts; those lower UI layers must not depend on compositions. Nothing under `client/ui` may directly or transitively depend on application state, runtime, shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, or domain state. Supply connected behavior through props or narrow host contracts and keep the adapter with its application, shell, or feature owner. Product-aware branding is an application adapter over portable brand assets. Do not move a domain-neutral composition merely because it currently has only one consumer. A portable-looking renderer such as breadcrumbs belongs in UI; route and resource resolution remain in a shell adapter. Capabilities may depend on lower-level runtime, DataFn, persistence, schema, and portable UI contracts, but never on application, feature, or product implementations. Add only named capability directories and explicit subpath imports; do not add a capabilities barrel or generic `shared`, `core`, `state`, or `stores` bucket. Use direct imports after moves, without compatibility wrappers. Shared runtime code must not transitively load capability or application implementations. Features use declared public entries when consuming another capability. Source aliases do not enforce package exports, so run the architecture checker. ## Commands Run commands from the repository root using npm workspaces and Turbo: ```sh npm ci --legacy-peer-deps npm run dev:nucleus npm run dev:memotron npm run dev:pointron npm run check:architecture node tools/check/type-ownership.mjs npm run check:apps npm --workspace @21n/account-service run typecheck npm run test npm run lint npm run build:nucleus npm run build:memotron-share ``` Use the Caddy HTTPS hosts and account-service health checks in `AGENTS.md` for local browser work. Run one product server and browser worker at a time when practical. Do not treat compiler success as browser, cloud, native-device, or deployment proof. ## Database changes Regenerate DataFn mappings with the account-service scripts. Generate and commit a forward migration for physical schema changes; never edit an applied migration. Deployment executes the checked-in migration journal. A successful local `datafn:push:local` does not prove that deployment migrations are complete. ## Review and delivery Preserve unrelated checkout changes. Review product configuration and callers before editing. Follow the existing-test and user-facing behavior approval rules in `AGENTS.md`. Keep code free of inline comments and document exported APIs with JSDoc. PR descriptions must identify changed behavior, relevant verification, and unverified environments. --- name: using-21nco-github description: Uses the thyaravind GitHub account for repositories under dev/n or with a 21nCo origin. Use for any GitHub CLI, pull request, issue, release, or repository operation in those repositories. --- # Using 21nCo GitHub For any repository whose path is under `dev/n` or whose Git remote belongs to `21nCo`: - Run every `gh` command with `GH_CONFIG_DIR=~/.config/gh-other`. - Verify `GH_CONFIG_DIR=~/.config/gh-other gh auth status` reports `thyaravind` as the active account before making changes. - Never use the default GitHub account or silently fall back to another account. - Use the existing `21nCo` remote for pushes. If `thyaravind` lacks permission, stop and report the denial instead of creating a fork or alternate remote.

# Applications | App | Website | Description | | -------- | ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Memotron | [memotron.app](https://memotron.app) | **Your memory atlas**, a tool for managing your digital memory and personal knowledge.
